## Overview Drop the redundant weight-tensor clones for loaders whose iterators already yield caller-owned tensors: `runai_safetensors_weights_iterator` with `runai-model-streamer>=0.17.1` (clone kept for older versions), and the pooling-model adapter probe for runai and the other owned-tensor load formats. ## Claims - `--load-format runai_streamer` no longer copies each weight tensor while loading, with `runai-model-streamer>=0.17.1`. - Older streamers keep working: the iterator clones for them, so buffer reuse cannot corrupt weights. - Pooling models no longer clone every weight in the `*ForCausalLM` / `*Model` prefix probe for runai, default safetensors/`pt`/`npcache`, `instanttensor`, `tensorizer`, `sharded_state` and `modelexpress`. - Minimum `runai-model-streamer` is now 0.17.1 in the extras, Docker image and requirements. ## Validation Released vLLM 0.32.0 wheel with this change applied on top (no compile), on CPU and on an H200 pod. ```bash pytest tests/models/test_adapters.py \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader/test_weight_utils.py ``` | Streamer | Result | Note | |---|---|---| | 0.17.1 | 13 passed (adapters + weight_utils, incl. `test_runai_model_loader`) | no clone, `owned=True` passed | | 0.16.1 | all pass except `..._yields_owned_tensors` | expected: clone fallback is used, test asserts no clone | - Mutation checks: always cloning fails `..._yields_owned_tensors`; dropping the fallback fails `..._streamer_versions`; removing `runai_streamer` from the whitelist fails the new adapter test; whitelisting `fastsafetensors` fails `test_pooling_load_weights_clones_probed_weights` and `test_pooling_prefix_probe_uses_hf_to_vllm_mapper`.
Full runai_streamer_loader/ directory run on Nebius 0.16.1: 40 failed, 25 passed, 1 skipped. 0.17.1: 39 failed, 26 passed, 1 skipped. The 39 shared failures are in `test_runai_model_streamer_loader.py` and come from the test setup, not this change: the 0.32.0 wheel's `runai_streamer_loader.py` has no `runai_pull_files` or `is_unused_weight`, which those tests patch. The only difference between the two versions is `..._yields_owned_tensors`.
Not yet measured: peak CPU memory and load time vs `main` for `--load-format runai_streamer`. ## Details **Root cause.** Before 0.17.1 the streamer can reuse its read buffers, so each tensor had to be cloned to stay valid. From 0.17.1, `stream_files(..., owned=True)` (the default) gives every yielded tensor to the caller and never reuses its memory, so the clone is a redundant copy. **Changes.** - `weight_utils.py`: pass `owned=True` when `stream_files` accepts it and yield tensors directly. Otherwise stream as before and clone. Detection is by the `owned` parameter, not a version string. - `adapters.py`: the probe cloned every weight because the iterator "may reuse the tensor buffer". It now clones only when `load_config.load_format` is not in `_OWNED_TENSOR_LOAD_FORMATS`. - Version bump to `>=0.17.1` in `setup.py`, `docker/`, and `requirements/test/xpu.{in,txt}` so new installs get the fast path - Tests: renamed the runai iterator test (now asserts no clone), added a fake-streamer test with and without `owned`, and an adapter test that whitelisted formats do not clone. **Whitelist.** `auto`, `hf`, `safetensors`, `mistral`, `pt`, `npcache`, `instanttensor` (`copy=True`), `tensorizer` (non-lazy deserializer caches independent tensors), `sharded_state`, `modelexpress` (delegates), `runai_streamer`, `runai_streamer_sharded`. `fastsafetensors` is excluded: 0.5.0 documents independent tensors, but 0.3.3 (the allowed minimum) only clones when `pg.size() == 1`. Custom or new load formats keep the clone until added. **Limitations.** Only the listed iterators were reviewed; model-specific `load_weights` code may still copy. Tests ran on the 0.32.0 wheel plus overlay, not a source build of this branch. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
